questions.def: "Hinge on" means to depend entirely on.
questions.question: The company's success hinged ___ securing the new contract.

questions.def: "Live down" means to repair a damaged reputation.
questions.question: After the scandal, he struggled to ___ his reputation.

questions.def: "Factor in" means to include something when making a calculation.
questions.question: The researchers ___ the environmental impact into their analysis.

questions.def: "Fall through" means to fail to happen.
questions.question: The project fell ___ due to lack of funding.

questions.def: "Gloss over" means to avoid discussing something.
questions.question: She tried to ___ the difficult topic during the meeting.

questions.def: "Iron out" means to resolve difficulties.
questions.question: The details will be ___ in the next stage.

questions.def: "Crack down" means to take severe measures.
questions.question: The government is trying to crack ___ on tax evasion.

questions.def: "Give rise to" means to cause something.
questions.question: The new policy will ___ a lot of debate.

questions.def: "Rule out" means to exclude something.
questions.question: The judge ___ the evidence inadmissible.

questions.def: "Delve into" means to investigate thoroughly.
questions.question: The scientist delved ___ the complexities of the phenomenon.

questions.def: "Fudge" (often with "over") means to avoid giving a clear answer.
questions.question: The politician tried to ___ the issue.

questions.def: "Eke out" means to barely manage to live.
questions.question: They managed to ___ a living from farming.

questions.def: "Shelve off" means to postpone indefinitely.
questions.question: The company shelved ___ the project due to budget constraints.

questions.def: "Hammer home" means to emphasize repeatedly.
questions.question: The speaker ___ the importance of education.

questions.def: "Siphon off" means to divert money illegally.
questions.question: The company was accused of ___ funds.

questions.def: "Turn up" means to be discovered unexpectedly.
questions.question: The investigation turned ___ some unexpected evidence.

questions.def: "Shore up" means to support or strengthen.
questions.question: The government is trying to ___ the economy.

questions.def: "Drum up" means to generate enthusiasm or support.
questions.question: They ___ support for the proposal.

questions.def: "Pan out" means to turn out well.
questions.question: The plan panned ___ better than expected.

questions.def: "Opt in" means to choose to participate.
questions.question: The company decided to ___ the new technology.

questions.def: "Hive off" means to separate or sell a business division.
questions.question: The company ___ several divisions.

questions.def: "Fend off" means to defend against an attack.
questions.question: The team had to fend ___ several attacks.

questions.def: "Dig into" means to investigate thoroughly.
questions.question: The journalist decided to ___ the story.

questions.def: "Fall through" means to fail to happen.
questions.question: The project fell ___ due to lack of funding.

questions.def: "Hive off" means to separate a part of a company.
questions.question: The company decided to ___ its less profitable division.

questions.def: "Account for" means to explain or justify something.
questions.question: The discrepancy can be ___ for by human error.

questions.def: "Fob off" means to deceive someone with inadequate answers.
questions.question: The politician tried to fob the public ___ with vague promises.

questions.def: "Close off" means to block or prevent access.
questions.question: The new regulations ___ several loopholes.

questions.def: "Square with" means to be consistent or in agreement with.
questions.question: The findings ___ with previous research.

questions.def: "Crack down on" means to take severe measures.
questions.question: The government is cracking ___ on tax evasion.
